text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Tariffs for railway transport are expected to rise starting May 1, the paper says.
- The SNCFR railway authority plans to cut up to 4,000 jobs over the next two months.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- A passenger train derailled in the county of Bacau but no victims or injuries were reported.
- Sales of fuel oil to the farming sector dropped by 40 percent.
- Ciprom SA and Sinterom Cluj wil be listed on the stock exchange.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The central bank bought 55 kilograms of gold from the population in March.
- The government decided to liberalise wheat exports starting August 15.
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development might be interested in a partnership with the National Oil Company, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- A new Hungarian consular office is due to open in the Transylvanian city of Cluj at the end of May.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Recent labour movements with workers staging protests and blocking roads are a real danger for Romania's economic and social stability, ex-president Ion Iliescu said. He said his Party of Social Democracy cannot advise people to cease protests, as long as their vital interests are "jeopardised."
- The country's audio-visual authority plans to ban films containing violent or erotic scenes, the newspaper says.
- Romania's failure to join NATO in a first wave of admission would lead to the formation of a new parliamentary majority, said Valeriu Tabara, leader of National Unity Party.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- A SNCFR official blamed the train derailment in the county of Bacau on the poor infrastructure, said. ($ = 7,072 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
